## Mobility modelling for infectious disease epidemiology

`nomad` provides fitted mobility models, source-data profiles, prediction checks,
uncertainty summaries and ensembles. The database includes 612 supplied Facebook
fits across 51 country/territory datasets and two original Zambia fits. Models,
public covariates and diagnostic plots are bundled for offline use.

## Installation

Install [JAGS 4.x](https://sourceforge.net/projects/mcmc-jags/files/JAGS/4.x/)
for the underlying `mobility` dependency, then install from GitHub. On macOS,
use the official JAGS 4.3.2 installer; the current rjags package requires JAGS 4:

```r
remotes::install_github("OJWatson/nomad", upgrade = FALSE)
```

This is a GitHub distribution; the complete model payload makes the source
package approximately 156 MiB. CRAN distribution is a separate future task.

## A first prediction

Start by finding a dataset with fitted models. Check its prediction period and
distance units before using it in a downstream analysis.

```{r}
library(nomad)
mobility_table(country = "COM")[, c(
  "name", "has_fitted_models", "prediction_period_days", "distance_unit"
)]
model <- model_db$com_fb_2025_mod_grav_exp
M <- predict(model, duration = 21)
round(M)
```

Rows are origins and columns are destinations; values are predicted trips over
21 days. For new regions, supply a named distance matrix and matching named
populations, declaring the distance units explicitly:

```r
predict(model, newdata = list(D = distances, N = populations), unit = "m", duration = 21)
```

Transferable models support new regions. Basic/finite radiation models support
their exact original setting only; unsupported requests fail with an explanation.
Original Zambia CDR/Facebook prediction periods remain unknown, so those models
can return unscaled predictions with a warning but cannot convert durations.

The [guided introduction](https://ojwatson.github.io/nomad/articles/introduction.html)
explains inputs and outputs. The
[model catalogue](https://ojwatson.github.io/nomad/articles/model.html) includes
source locations, availability and diagnostics. The
[selection walkthrough](https://ojwatson.github.io/nomad/articles/selecting-a-model.html)
covers uncertainty, ensembles and `compare_models()`, an interactive weight slider.
The outbreak example holds transmission assumptions fixed while comparing mobility.

## Provenance and maintenance

JHU supplied the new Facebook data/model archives. The fitting recipes are in
`data-raw/functions/facebook_models.R` and the country scripts under
`data-raw/models`. Imports preserve the supplied parameters. Private Facebook
trip matrices are excluded; saved diagnostics remain available.

Kenya 2009, Namibia 2014 and Burkina Faso 2016 CDR datasets remain catalogued with
`has_fitted_models = FALSE` until their data or fitted models become available.
